GeneDef:DMS_Gene_FrogmanGestation.name: DMS_Gene_FrogmanGestation
GeneDef:DMS_Gene_FrogmanGestation.label: frogman gestation
GeneDef:DMS_Gene_FrogmanGestation.description:
The directed development sequence of an XM132 artificial military organism. Written into an embryo, it overrides normal gestation entirely: the mesonuclear substrate lays down a sealed synthetic-mechanical frame in place of human tissue, and drives itself toward one fixed adult form without any external guidance.

A carrier brought to term produces a biomatroid larva rather than a child. The larva forms a gestation pod around itself and finishes developing outside the womb.

The sequence is inert in any other context. It cannot be inherited or expressed in a living body.

Colonial fleet law lists AMO development sequences as prohibited articles. Manufacture, transfer and use carry the same sentence, and fleets destroy production chains found on settled worlds rather than seize them.

ThingDef:DMS_SynthFormingPod.name: DMS_SynthFormingPod
ThingDef:DMS_SynthFormingPod.label: gestation pod
ThingDef:DMS_SynthFormingPod.description: A biomatroid larva sealed inside the mineral pod it formed around itself after birth. Development continues inside: muscle bundles lay down over the frame, the outer seal cures, and the control lattice organizes itself. The mesonuclear substrate runs the whole process on its own, and needs no power, feedstock or supervision.\n\nThe pod swells as the larva matures, and flexes in wind. It cannot defend itself, and breaking it destroys the biomatroid inside. It is light enough to be uninstalled and carried elsewhere.

Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_BionicSho.name: DMS_Info_BionicShock
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_BionicSho.label: xeno limb syndrome
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_BionicSho.description:
Neurally interfaced prostheses have no biological receptors, so the nervous system never fully accepts them. Every installed prosthesis periodically triggers xeno limb syndrome: the first episode starts at LV.1, and each later episode pushes the existing syndrome up one level. The more prostheses a patient carries, the faster it worsens.

The syndrome has five levels, progressing from itching and pain through mental breaks to coma. Worsening beyond LV.5 is fatal.

Treatment: each dose of neuroglue lowers the syndrome by one level, curing it outright at LV.1. While neuroglue is in effect, the syndrome cannot worsen.

Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Synthetic.name: DMS_Info_SyntheticRejection
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Synthetic.label: synthetic rejection
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Synthetic.description:
The host's immune system never fully accepts biosynthetic tissue. Each installed biosynthetic part independently triggers synthetic rejection, on average once every 40 days.

An episode lasts 5 days, bringing fever and pain, slightly dulled consciousness and severely impaired blood filtration.

Treatment: a single dose of neuroglue cures it at once, and any episode that begins while neuroglue is in effect clears up immediately.

Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Neuroglue.name: DMS_Info_Neuroglue
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Neuroglue.label: neuroglue therapy
Fortified.FFF_InfoDef:DMS_Info_Neuroglue.description:
Each dose takes effect immediately:
 - xeno limb syndrome is lowered by one level, or cured outright at LV.1.

While neuroglue is in effect (about 5.5 days):
 - xeno limb syndrome cannot worsen;
 - synthetic rejection and phantom limb syndrome are cured, and clear up immediately if they recur;
 - the patient cannot contract fibrous or sensory mechanites.

Side effect: mild pain for the duration.

QuestScriptDef:DMS_CourtMartial.name: DMS_CourtMartial
QuestScriptDef:DMS_CourtMartial.xml:
DMS_CourtMartial DMS_QuestSuccess_Ceremony DMS_QuestFailed_Ceremony 1 0 2 6~10
  • questName->Court-martial: [defendant_nameFull]
  • questName->Military tribunal summons
  • questName->Fleet judicial notice
    •
  • questDescription(defendantRanked==True)->A sergeant of the military police command of [issuerFactionName], [asker_nameFull], has issued a notice over the public band, expressing [asker_possessive] strictly-official concern over the recent military-diplomatic incident caused by [playerFactionName]. As [playerFactionName] counts enlisted personnel of [issuerFactionName] among its members, [asker_pronoun] intends to settle the matter through formal court-martial proceedings.\n\nBy [asker_possessive] account, the highest-ranking officer of [playerFactionName], [defendant_nameFull], must report to the fleet's local military tribunal for investigation and questioning. Should [playerFactionName] cooperate, [asker_pronoun] will immediately requisition an orbital transport to collect [defendant_nameDef], and hostilities between [issuerFactionName] and [playerFactionName] will be suspended for the duration.\n\n[asker_nameDef] tells us the investigation will conclude within [investigationDays] days, after which the accused will answer for the charges in court, the verdict to be pronounced by the [issuerFactionName] Navigation Hall and executed at once. If [defendant_nameDef] cooperates, [defendant_possessive] punishment will be weighed leniently, though given the gravity of a military incident, it will still mean short-term detention and a demotion at the very least.\n\nRoom, board and medical care during [defendant_possessive] sentence will be borne by [issuerFactionName], and [defendant_pronoun] will be returned to [playerFactionName] once it is served.
  • questDescription(defendantRanked==True)->Over the public band, [asker_nameFull], a duty sergeant of the [issuerFactionName] military police command, has served us formal notice: the recent military-diplomatic incident attributed to [playerFactionName] will not be ignored. Because members of [playerFactionName] remain on the [issuerFactionName] service roll, [asker_pronoun] insists the affair be resolved before a proper court-martial rather than on a battlefield.\n\nThe terms are plain. Our highest-ranking officer, [defendant_nameFull], is to submit to investigation and questioning at the fleet's local tribunal. Upon our agreement, [asker_pronoun] will requisition an orbital transport for [defendant_nameDef] without delay, and [issuerFactionName] will hold its guns for as long as the proceedings run.\n\nPer [asker_nameDef], the inquiry closes within [investigationDays] days; the accused will then speak in [defendant_possessive] own defense before the bench, and the Navigation Hall of [issuerFactionName] will pass sentence for immediate execution. Cooperation buys leniency, but a military incident of this weight carries no less than brief detention and one grade of demotion.\n\nThe fleet will feed, house and treat [defendant_nameDef] throughout the sentence, and return [defendant_pronoun] to [playerFactionName] when it ends.
  • questDescription(defendantRanked==True)->[asker_nameFull], sergeant of the military police command, [issuerFactionName], has broadcast an official communiqué regarding the military-diplomatic incident recently caused by [playerFactionName]. [asker_pronoun] frames it as nothing personal, merely procedure: since [playerFactionName] harbors personnel still enrolled with [issuerFactionName], the matter falls under military jurisdiction and must go before a court-martial.\n\n[asker_pronoun] requires that [defendant_nameFull], the senior rank-holder of [playerFactionName], attend the fleet's local tribunal for investigation and questioning. The moment we consent, an orbital transport will be requisitioned to carry [defendant_nameDef] up, and [issuerFactionName] will suspend all hostilities against [playerFactionName] pending judgment.\n\nAs [asker_nameDef] lays it out: [investigationDays] days of investigation, then the accused argues [defendant_possessive] defense in open court, and the [issuerFactionName] Navigation Hall pronounces sentence on the spot. Willing cooperation will be weighed in mitigation, but the minimum remains short-term detention plus demotion by one grade.\n\nQuarters, rations and medical care during the sentence come at [issuerFactionName]'s expense; [defendant_pronoun] will be shipped back to [playerFactionName] on release.
  • questDescription(defendantRanked==False)->A sergeant of the military police command of [issuerFactionName], [asker_nameFull], has issued a notice over the public band, expressing [asker_possessive] strictly-official concern over the recent military-diplomatic incident caused by [playerFactionName]. No member of [playerFactionName] holds a commission [asker_pronoun] could act against, so [asker_pronoun] intends to proceed against the settlement itself, through formal court-martial proceedings.\n\nBy [asker_possessive] account, [playerFactionName] must surrender the member it can least afford to lose, [defendant_nameFull], to the fleet's local military tribunal for investigation and questioning. Should [playerFactionName] cooperate, [asker_pronoun] will immediately requisition an orbital transport to collect [defendant_nameDef], and hostilities between [issuerFactionName] and [playerFactionName] will be suspended for the duration.\n\n[asker_nameDef] tells us the investigation will conclude within [investigationDays] days, after which the accused will answer for the charges in court, the verdict to be pronounced by the [issuerFactionName] Navigation Hall and executed at once. There is no rank here to reduce, so nothing can be taken off in mitigation: the sentence is detention, and the whole of it.\n\nRoom, board and medical care during [defendant_possessive] sentence will be borne by [issuerFactionName], and [defendant_pronoun] will be returned to [playerFactionName] once it is served.
  • questDescription(defendantRanked==False)->Over the public band, [asker_nameFull], a duty sergeant of the [issuerFactionName] military police command, has served us formal notice: the recent military-diplomatic incident attributed to [playerFactionName] will not be ignored. Upon our agreement, [asker_pronoun] will requisition an orbital transport for [defendant_nameDef] without delay, and [issuerFactionName] will hold its guns for as long as the proceedings run.\n\nPer [asker_nameDef], the inquiry closes within [investigationDays] days; the accused will then speak in [defendant_possessive] own defense before the bench, and the Navigation Hall of [issuerFactionName] will pass sentence for immediate execution. With no grade to strip, leniency has nothing to work with: the sentence is detention, and the full term of it.\n\nThe fleet will feed, house and treat [defendant_nameDef] throughout the sentence, and return [defendant_pronoun] to [playerFactionName] when it ends.

The moment we consent, an orbital transport will be requisitioned to carry [defendant_nameDef] up, and [issuerFactionName] will suspend all hostilities against [playerFactionName] pending judgment.\n\nAs [asker_nameDef] lays it out: [investigationDays] days of investigation, then the accused argues [defendant_possessive] defense in open court, and the [issuerFactionName] Navigation Hall pronounces sentence on the spot. ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_QubitDe.name: DMS_Occultech_QubitDecryption
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_QubitDe.label: qubit decryption
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_QubitDe.description:
A decoding technique that bypasses a stele's own verification layer and reads its data by directly measuring the quantum state held at each lattice site of its holographic storage plates. The stele's encryption rests on the assumption that no one outside the fleets can observe those quantum states without collapsing them; this technique simply chooses to accept the collapse. Every reading permanently destroys the region it reads. What is recovered can be archived for research, and what is lost can never be restored.
The technique was leaked by fleet deviants. Steles are the backup memory of every colonial world, and every stele scanned this way is a record that no one will ever be able to read again.

Approved by ████ and ███, qubit decryption and its related technologies are designated class II sealed technology. Disclosure of such technology is prohibited, and any decoding equipment discovered is to be destroyed on site.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_BionicS.name: DMS_Occultech_BionicSuitHeavy
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_BionicS.label: enclosed assault frame
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_BionicS.description:
A load-bearing frame anchored directly into the pilot's skeleton, driven by artificial muscle bundles that only draw at full closure. It allows a single soldier to carry and operate armament far beyond their own muscular limit. Because closure is a precondition of output, the device cannot be released by any conventional means once sealed, and separation of the pilot must be performed surgically.
This inability to self-release classifies the device, under the laws of war, as restraining equipment upon its own pilot. The positive applications of its skeletal anchoring and load-transfer principles to prosthetic rehabilitation are nonetheless equally present.

Approved by ███████ and ███, the enclosed assault frame and its related technologies are designated class I sealed technology. Sale of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and its related technologies are to be progressively declassified once a colonial world's society attains class I standard.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Remnant.name: DMS_Occultech_RemnantPatterns
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Remnant.label: garrison arsenal
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Remnant.description:
A line of self-supervising sentry weapons built for long-term garrison duty: a quadruped garrison mech for installation security, a large drone platform that flies cover for unmanned mother-drones, and an automated nest that launches FPV suicide drones at intruders. All three were designed specifically for pioneer colonization operations, which needed defenses able to hold a world alone for decades before the fleet arrived, so all three carry fallback directives in their control cores that keep them executing their last standing order until the chassis fails.
Under the laws of war, weapons that outlast the conflict they were deployed for are classed alongside minefields. The remnants still guarding this world's beacons and installations are what these patterns become once their makers are gone.

Approved by ████ and ███, the garrison arsenal and its related technologies are designated class I sealed technology. Sale of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and its related technologies are to be progressively declassified once a colonial world's society attains class I standard.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Hydraul.name: DMS_Occultech_HydraulicFracturing
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Hydraul.label: hydraulic fracturing
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Hydraul.description:
Ultra-high-pressure fluid tears the deep bedrock apart and frees the hydrocarbons and rare volatiles trapped in fissures in the crust. Even long after the surface deposits are exhausted, it keeps drawing chemfuel and minerals from underground. The mineral-laden slurry the process discharges, however, leaves severe heavy-metal pollution all around it.
As a means of resource extraction its industrial efficiency is extremely high, but spreading the technique across industrial worlds that lack environmental ethics can degrade a planet's living conditions rapidly, to the point that it is no longer habitable.

Approved by ████ and ██, hydraulic fracturing extraction and its related technologies are designated class I sealed technology. Sale of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and its related technologies are to be progressively declassified once a colonial world's society attains class I standard.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Frogman.name: DMS_Occultech_Frogman
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Frogman.label: directed chassis gestation
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_Frogman.description:
A sealed technique that cultivates artificial military organisms in place of printing mechs. A directed development sequence is written into an embryo, whose mesonuclear substrate then lays down synthetic-mechanical structure instead of biological tissue and matures on its own. The embryo is brought to term in a growth vat.

Further AMO development was stopped for good after a catastrophic incident in the Earth era. Self-developing military organisms do enormous harm to local society and productive capacity, and the technology has been proscribed ever since. The colonial fleets carry out the sanctions under this ban themselves, never through local authorities.

Unlocks the XM132 Frogman and its development sequence.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_MainBat.name: DMS_Occultech_MainBattle
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_MainBat.label: main battle specification
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_MainBat.description:
The design and production technology behind the total-war specification mechs and related equipment that the colonial fleets field against planet-scale hostile organizations and harmful entities. The manufacturing process of these mechs has been drastically simplified so that they serve better as high-performance weapons, produced and expended without pause over the course of a total war. Their performance, however, does not come from nowhere.
After the main battle specification leak on colonial world ████, colonial fleets across sector ████ observed similar technology reaching interstellar pirates and spacefaring military regimes through arms dealers. The technology recovery programs each fleet carried out after the incident proved effective, and the main battle specification was sealed again after ████.

To prevent such an incident from happening again, however, approved by ████ and ██, the main battle specification and its related technologies are designated class II sealed technology. Provision of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and outside emergency war mobilization, standing ground-force deployments are to avoid employing it in any military operation.

ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_ZeroPoi.name: DMS_Occultech_ZeroPoint
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_ZeroPoi.label: zero-point energy
ResearchProjectDef:DMS_Occultech_ZeroPoi.description: Draws energy from the quantum fluctuations of the vacuum itself. Once the principle is mastered, antiparticles can be consumed to produce solidified zero-point energy, which powers the most advanced machines and weapons. It is the threshold of transcendent technology. But the true cost of harnessing the void is something humanity has yet to fully understand.\n\nAfter the main battle ███ division that landed on planet ████ drove the transcendent machine ████ out of the planet's crust, where it had lain parasitic, in the year ████, colonial fleet ████ compiled a detailed account of how such transcendent beings are constituted and passed it by stele to the other colonial fleets operating in the Andromeda cluster. Because transcendent beings and their applications still contaminate the physical universe in ways that remain largely beyond control, disclosure of such technology to developing worlds is prohibited, and its related preventive technologies are to be declassified once a colonial world's society attains class II standard.

ThingDef:DMS_OccultTechFont.name: DMS_OccultTechFont
ThingDef:DMS_OccultTechFont.label: Stele
ThingDef:DMS_OccultTechFont.description: A databank holding technical data and backups of colonial records, along with case analyses and post-incident reviews of every accident that has occurred across all colonization programs to date. A stele serves both as the medium through which the colonial fleets share experience and knowledge with their kin across star systems, and as a backup database buried deep beneath every colonized world. Complex encryption and verification algorithms keep its records from being lost over long voyages through space or ages sealed underground, while also preventing anyone outside the colonial fleets from obtaining the dangerous technology within.\n\nRumor has it that decoding techniques leaked by fleet deviants can perform a destructive scan to extract the data inside, but using such techniques may draw the hostility of the colonial fleets.

ThingDef:DMS_OccultechExtractor.name: DMS_OccultechExtractor
ThingDef:DMS_OccultechExtractor.label: Decoder
ThingDef:DMS_OccultechExtractor.description: A destructive decoding rig. It fires a high-energy laser through the holographic storage plates inside a stele and analyzes the scattered spectrum to read the data within: the only way for factions outside the colonial fleets to access a stele's contents. Set it flush against a stele and supply power, and it will continuously extract the knowledge and file it into your expeditional research, no researcher required. Extraction stops if the stele runs dry, power is lost, or no stele is in front of it. It can be uninstalled and reinstalled elsewhere.

ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Frogman.name: DMS_Mech_Frogman
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Frogman.label: Frogman
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Frogman.description:
The XM132 Frogman is the earliest artificial military organism on known record. Its mesonuclear biological design lets it be cultured in any environment and develop itself into designated adult.

In the Earth era, such biomatroid AMOs represented was briefly held to be the technology that would replace synthetic mechs and conventional mechanoids alike. A single severe incident ended that line of development for good.

The adult form is humanlike. It grows its own highly sealed composite plasfibre integument and a closed-loop internal cooling system. Every joint cavity is pressure-compensated and packed with dielectric gel, so it can swim in, wade ashore and go straight into combat. Earth-era marine corps used them for beach reconnaissance, harbour demolition and boarding actions.

AMO technology is tightly controlled under the colonial fleet programme. That is why a bioweapon this well suited to local conditions remains a rare sight across the rim.

ThingDef:DMS_Gun_RecoillessLight.name: DMS_Gun_RecoillessLight
ThingDef:DMS_Gun_RecoillessLight.label: light recoilless rifle
ThingDef:DMS_Gun_RecoillessLight.description: A four-kilogram disposable recoilless launcher, issued down to squad level as a throwaway answer to armor, bunkers and doorways. The fibre-wound tube is discarded once fired, and its fire control unit accepts four interchangeable warheads, so the operator picks the effect before the tube ever reaches the shoulder.\n\nIt is light enough for a scout drone to carry, and its shaped-charge warhead defeats plating far above its own weight class, while the demolition and screening rounds let a single trooper open a wall or cover a withdrawal. The cost is that everything is spent in one shot: no reload, a short effective range, and a backblast signature that tells every gun on the field where the operator is standing.

ThingDef:DMS_SensibilityBlocker.description: A highly concentrated neuro-targeted agent that suppresses the receptors behind affective thought. Outwardly, the subject's aversion to their surroundings all but vanishes for as long as it lasts, which once made it a standard combat drug for exoskeleton pilots on long missions. Subjects keep a complete memory of the experience after it wears off, however, and once it was found to cause possible sensory loss its use was gradually banned.\n\nTemporarily suspends secondary needs such as beauty, comfort, outdoors, indoors and space, and negates the mood penalties of environment-related thoughts.

ThingDef:DMS_CommandCoprocessor.label: Command Coprocessor
ThingDef:DMS_CommandCoprocessor.description:
An auxiliary processing board fitted alongside a command automatroid's core processor. It takes over the signal multiplexing and unit bookkeeping that would otherwise occupy the main processor, letting the automatroid keep more units on its command chain at once.

The extra silicon draws power continuously, slightly increasing the automatroid's energy consumption.

Only command-type automatroids have a processor bus that can accept it.

ThingDef:DMS_BF_RecoillessRifle.label: Recoilless rifle rack
ThingDef:DMS_BF_RecoillessRifle.description: A pair of 65mm recoilless tubes on a shared cradle, built to bolt onto the side pylons of a battle frame. Line units fit it for one reason: a frame's own light armament has no answer to plating or a prepared firing position, and a walking mount can carry the tube into ground a two-man crew would never reach.\n\nLoaded with shaped-charge rockets, the rack defeats armor and fortifications far above the frame's weight class, and its fire control unit reloads a spent tube from carried stores between engagements. The frame pays for it in walking pace, dodging room and cargo allowance, and every backblast marks its position for every observer on the field.

  • questDescription(installation==DMS_SageNodeSite)->We have found the host that is coordinating [fleetName]'s hunt for us: a SAGE node, the distributed strategic command computer the fleet uses for planetary air defense and to tie together the radar and navigation networks across several continents. Its rack array is guarded by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat), and it is wired into a full facility alarm system with fire support.\n\nThe SAGE core can be hacked two or three times. Each run pulls technical blueprints, sealed data caches or access keys out of its strategic database, and each run will set off the facility's alarm again. Destroying it will cripple the fleet's hunt; within a year or two another computer on the SAGE network will be promoted to host and pick up where it left off.\n\nThe node's coordinates hold for [siteTimeout], until the network rotates its hosts.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown, and the node can call in mortar fire.

  • questDescription(installation==DMS_VaultStationSite)->A supply manifest recovered from remnant traffic lists a [siteFactionName] storage vault, and the surface station that sits on top of it. The station is still manned by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat), and heavy units are among them.\n\nThe freight elevator into the vault is locked under an armored cover plate, slaved to the access console beside it. The console takes a key-card, not a hack: swipe one and the plate retracts. The car still has power, so what is below was never collected.\n\nThe manifest's location fix expires in [siteTimeout]. After that the station will relocate and its position will be lost.\n\nThe installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown. Get the shaft open, then decide whether to hold the surface or go down.
  • questDescription(installation==DMS_RepairStationSite)->A maintenance request on the remnant network leads to a [siteFactionName] field repair depot. The depot is guarded by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat): engineers, riflemen and a drone screen.\n\nTwo units are still clamped in the depot's cradles, in hibernation, behind a sealed maintenance door. They were never re-authenticated after servicing, so a mechanitor with spare bandwidth can hack one and take it. The depot's security console releases the door. There is also a mobile crew lifter on the pad and a stock of tungsteel in the stores.\n\nThe request's location fix expires in [siteTimeout]. After that the depot will relocate and its position will be lost.\n\nThe installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.
  • questDescription(installation==DMS_OperationBaseSite)->Remnant traffic has given away a [siteFactionName] forward operating base. It is held by (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat): line infantry behind the wire, with heavy support and night-capable units in reserve.\n\nThe base is a supply hub. Crates of rations, small arms, spare parts and prosthetics sit in the open, and a freight elevator at the back of the compound leads down into a buried store. The blast doors in front of it answer to two security consoles; hack both to open the way, then hack the lift itself.\n\nThe position fix holds for [siteTimeout]. After that the base will strike camp and its position will be lost.\n\nThe installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.
  • questDescription(installation==DMS_SiteStationSite)->A pre-war station, half of it collapsed, has been located nearby. A [siteFactionName] detachment has dug into the ruins: (*Threat)[enemiesCount] [enemiesLabel](/Threat), shield-bearers and infantry with drone and lifter support, spread across the station's halls.\n\nThe station was abandoned in a hurry. Ancient supply crates, industrial shelving and the wrecks of the old security systems are still scattered through it, along with a working pod launcher pair. Everything the detachment has not already stripped is yours.\n\nThe detachment is expected to move on in [siteTimeout]. After that the station will be picked clean and no longer worth the trip.\n\nThe installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.\n\nOne of the station's freight elevators still runs down to a data archive the fleet buried beneath it. A facility server core sits in the sealed server hall at the bottom; it can be hacked several times, and every attempt will bring the archive's defences up from below. The corridors are fitted with gas vents, and a lockdown controller will seal the lift a minute after the alert level maxes out.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, its monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown, and the station is large enough to get lost in.
  • questDescription(installation==DMS_LaunchSiteSite)->An old missile launch complex has turned up on the scanners. Wrecked automatroids, a logistics container, sensor and radar mounts and the remains of the launch crews' equipment are all still where they fell.\n\nThe patrol's schedule puts it there for another [siteTimeout]. After that it moves on and the site's position is lost.\n\nThe installation also runs a site server: a small records host that can be hacked once for blueprints or access keys, at the cost of setting off the alarm.\n\nCaution: it is a hostile installation. Once you enter, the patrol's monitoring protocol will summon enemy reinforcements after a countdown.

ThingDef:DMS_Building_BlastScanner.name: DMS_Building_BlastScanner
ThingDef:DMS_Building_BlastScanner.label: blast scanner
ThingDef:DMS_Building_BlastScanner.description:
A precision geological survey device. A mortar shell loaded into its charge chamber drives a seismic shockwave deep into the ground, and the device reads the returning echoes to map ore deposits far below the surface. One charge maps several deep deposits at once.

Surveying this way is never quiet. The shockwave all but inevitably wakes insect colonies dormant underground, and they tend to dig their way out close to whatever disturbed them.

Load a high-explosive shell, then light the fuse. The device needs time to recalibrate between charges.

ThingDef:DMS_ZeroPointGenerator.name: DMS_ZeroPointGenerator
ThingDef:DMS_ZeroPointGenerator.label: zero-point generator core
ThingDef:DMS_ZeroPointGenerator.description:
A complex device that punches a hole in real space through the controlled release of antigrain energy, drawing inexhaustible energy from the quantum fluctuations outside and condensing it into solid energy blocks for convenient storage and further processing.

Since the rim generally lacks antigrain production technology, the device usually has to rely on ready-made antigrain warheads as the catalyst that starts it running.

While powered, each antigrain warhead loaded as catalyst yields 25 units of solidified zero-point energy, one every 2.4 days. A single warhead keeps the core running for about a year.

ThingDef:DMS_Anchor.name: DMS_Anchor
ThingDef:DMS_Anchor.label: reality anchor
ThingDef:DMS_Anchor.description: A stabilization device that uses counter-technology to keep the surrounding space free from the influence of transcendent forces. To an ordinary person it is nothing more than a harmless decoration, but psycasters and transcendent artifacts find it hard to establish connections beyond this dimension in its presence, and cannot manifest their transcendent properties.\n\nWhile powered, it holds a stabilized field around itself. Inside it, no creature's capacities or physical limits can exceed 120% of normal, psycasts cannot be cast and invisibility fails. Anomalous entities and mutants are suppressed: slowed, weakened and far easier to contain. The field makes no distinction between friend and foe.

ThingDef:DMS_FacilityServerCore.name: DMS_FacilityServerCore
ThingDef:DMS_FacilityServerCore.label: facility server core
ThingDef:DMS_FacilityServerCore.description: A sizable transistor computer. Old but extremely reliable, machines like this serve as paperless office and records hosts throughout the colony fleet's facilities. A special radioisotope cell inside keeps it running for years without anyone tending it.\n\nThe lower data layers of these server cores usually hold backups of important technical blueprints and access key records. Breaking into it will inevitably set off the whole facility's alarm response, so it is best to prepare your defenses before you start hacking.

ThingDef:DMS_SageCore.name: DMS_SageCore
ThingDef:DMS_SageCore.label: SAGE
ThingDef:DMS_SageCore.description: A distributed strategic command computer that can take on auxiliary racks without limit, adding computing power as demand grows. The colony fleet uses it for planetary strategic air defense and to link the countless radar tracking and navigation networks spread across several continents. Destroying it is certain to cripple the fleet's hunting operations on the planet, though within a year or two another computer in the SAGE network will be promoted to host and carry on the task.\n\nIts lower storage still keeps copies of parts of the strategic database. Hacking it will bring the whole facility's alarm system down on you.

ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Gravekeeper.name: DMS_Mech_Gravekeeper
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Gravekeeper.label: gravekeeper
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_Gravekeeper.description:
A highly intelligent large automatroid, deployed by the colonial fleets specifically to patrol and guard important unmanned installations. Its parts are largely interchangeable with the mobile dragoon's, and it pairs excellent close-quarters combat ability with a formidable weapon system. The gravekeeper's design dates back to the lunar war of independence after the Universal Century, when most of the fighting took place in the narrow, enclosed tunnels of underground cities. Heavily armored mechs like the gravekeeper and the siegebreaker, carrying heavy weapons and able to suppress at close range, became the spearhead of both sides' fight for control of those tunnels.
Because of this specialized design, gravekeepers usually hold a defense in groups of five. Since they must patrol unattended installations for centuries, their rules of engagement are more conservative than an ordinary mech's, so that failing mechanisms do not trigger by mistake mid-mission. As a result, they will not leave their installation to engage an enemy on their own.

This pattern carries no shoulder rack.

Heavily armored mechs like the gravekeeper and the siegebreaker, carrying heavy weapons and able to suppress at close range, became the spearhead of both sides' fight for control of those tunnels.
Because of this specialized design, gravekeepers usually hold a defense in groups of five. Since they must patrol unattended installations for centuries, their rules of engagement are more conservative than an ordinary mech's, so that failing mechanisms do not trigger by mistake mid-mission. As a result, they will not leave their installation to engage an enemy on their own.

This configuration mounts the Gecko's Flameblaster on its shoulder for clearing corridors.

The [skillName] instruction on record runs well past the standard for the grade.

RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Hyrax.description: Gestate a hyrax Automatroid, an unmanned vehicle mounting a remote weapon station on a light tracked chassis. RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Dogge.name: DMS_Make_Dogge
RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Dogge.label: Gestate Dogge
RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Dogge.description: Gestate a Dogge Automatroid, a four-legged machine gun platform. The synthetic muscle bundles in its limbs give it uncommon cross-country mobility, and its low profile suits it to providing accompanying fire across open ground - it is usually used to mop up routed enemies and for counter-guerrilla work.\n\nIt keeps both an auto-engaging fixed machine gun turret and a separate weapon hardpoint that will take a flamethrower for close work, and it moves fast enough to keep pace with any advance. Culturing the synthetic muscle is expensive, its plating only handles fragments and small calibers, and the hardpoint will not accept a long-barrelled weapon. The Dogge is well suited to running down fast-moving light guerrillas and escaping prisoners, and it can also carry anti-tank rockets to punch above its weight in street fighting.

RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Grenadier.label: Gestate Grenadier
RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Grenadier.description: Gestate a Grenadier Automatroid, the indirect-fire control variant of the Soldat. Its fire control unit has been recalibrated to compute ballistic arcs, letting it operate grenade launchers, thrown ordnance and mortar mounts, and handle targets behind cover that direct fire cannot reach.\n\nIt is the most efficient mass-produced platform for clearing fortified positions and demolishing structures, and it carries a built-in flash launcher for suppression. In exchange it demands tungsteel and synthetic fabric to build, costs two points of bandwidth, and defends itself badly at direct range; it also inherits the Soldat's thin plating and exposed battery pack. Indirect fire does not distinguish friend from foe - deploy it behind your own units.

RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Sergeant.name: DMS_Make_Sergeant
RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Sergeant.label: Gestate Sergeant
RecipeDef:DMS_Make_Sergeant.description: Gestate a Sergeant Automatroid, the relay-command conversion of the Soldat, recognizable by the dish-shaped omnidirectional radar and transceiver mast on its back. Its job is to organize scattered units into a combined automatroid battlegroup (CAB), and to hold the command chain open on behalf of the mechanitor when they cannot move up in person.\n\nIts relay radius far exceeds the Noctula's and extends control into neighboring maps, and the identification code on its T/R transceiver can be used to request Soldat and Falcon reinforcement drops from synchronous orbit. The mass and processing load of the radar assembly cost four times the Soldat's bandwidth, however, and leave it slower, thinner-skinned, and able to carry nothing heavier than a sidearm for self-defense. When a Sergeant is destroyed, every link in the command chain it was holding open goes down with it.

ThingDef:DMS_AutomaticGrenadeLauncher.description:
A handheld automatic grenade launcher for clearing out clustered targets.

This weapon is specially designed for automatroid use, normal humans will struggle to use it without external equipment or augmentations.

Its tripod folds under the receiver, so a drafted operator can set it down into a firing position on the spot and break it back down just as quickly.

ThingDef:DMS_Turret_Sentry.label: Sentry gun
ThingDef:DMS_Turret_Sentry.description: A light automatic turret with a built-in battery, designed to be carried and set up wherever the line needs a gun. On the power grid it charges its internal cell; cut off from the grid it draws on that reserve and keeps firing until the cell runs dry. Switching it off puts it on standby: it stops watching and pours the saved power into the cell instead, charging twice as fast.\n\nIts tripod folds flat, so a drafted operator can pick it up, carry it forward and drop it into position on the spot. A cell charged before departure will keep it standing watch for days.

ThingDef:DMS_Mech_HermitCrab.name: DMS_Mech_HermitCrab
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_HermitCrab.label: Hermit Crab
ThingDef:DMS_Mech_HermitCrab.description: These large, expensive, and heavy mobile industrial machines are designed to be an all-in-one unit for colonizing new worlds. Their large and expensive magnetic stabilized shells integrate many complex-axis CNC tools and precision machinery, and the same stabilisation field doubles as a short-ranged projectile interceptor - a side effect the manufacturers were happy to advertise. In a pinch, its precision tools allow it to perform surgical procedures as long as the patient overcomes their fear of a machine weighing several tons acting as their surgeon. The shell also houses an engineering drone bay, letting it carry and deploy uca and erima work drones in the field.
